notes:
Refers specifically to the outer corner of the eye (temple side). An important body-part term in Japanese, as it appears frequently in descriptions of facial expressions, cosmetics, and aging.

The expression {目尻|めじり}を{下|さ}げる (to lower the outer corners of the eyes) describes a warm, affectionate smile or a doting expression — it is one of the most common uses of this word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目尻|めじり}を{下|さ}げる: to smile warmly, to have a doting look
- {目尻|めじり}のしわ: crow's feet, wrinkles at the eye corners
- {目尻|めじり}を{上|あ}げる: to raise the outer eye corners (showing anger or sharpness)
- {目尻|めじり}に{涙|なみだ}: tears at the corner of the eye

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {目頭|めがしら}: inner corner of the eye — the opposite location, near the nose
- まぶた: eyelid — the movable skin covering the eye
- {目元|めもと}: area around the eyes — a broader term for the eye area in general

definitions.explanation: the outer corner of the eye, near the temple; the area where the upper and lower eyelids meet on the side away from the nose

examples.english: There are wrinkles at the corners of the eyes.

examples.japanese: {目尻|めじり}を{下|さ}げて{笑|わら}った。
examples.english: She smiled with the corners of her eyes lowered.

examples.japanese: {目尻|めじり}にアイラインを{引|ひ}くと{目|め}が{大|おお}きく{見|み}える。
examples.english: If you draw eyeliner at the outer corners, your eyes look bigger.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{感動|かんどう}して{目尻|めじり}に{涙|なみだ}を{浮|う}かべていた。
examples.english: He was so moved that tears welled up at the corners of his eyes.
